Findings.Title: Infeasible optional safety projection aborts an ordinary heat
Findings.Expectation: A supported four-gate ordinary heat either completes through safe verified requests or handles infeasible alternatives explicitly; optional projection failure does not abort the heat.
Findings.Observation: Coupled time solve failure escapes SafetyProject before the first segment commits, in both forward and reversed input order and without an observer.
Findings.NumericalOrTraceEvidence: All pre-failure riders retain zero elapsed time/speed/progress. TimeSolveDiscontinuityException: Coupled time solve did not converge within its bound. Stack: SafetyProject -> ResolveProduction -> ResolveMovingRider -> ExecutedPathTraversal.Solve.
Findings.Subsystem: ContestedSpaceInteractionCoordinator safety feasibility boundary; ExecutedPathTraversal bounded solve
Findings.Confidence: High for the escaping failure and reproduction; specific failed alternative/root discontinuity needs the focused future investigation.
Findings.FuturePRScope: Explicit infeasible optional projection result, safe frozen-request handling and selected-execution failure contract. Preserve #61 caches and bounds; no substitute physics or raised tolerance.

Findings.Title: Partial canonical position fails the next segment handoff
Findings.Expectation: Valid partial positions accepted by the existing fixture factory advance to the intended next segment in both projection and execution.
Findings.Observation: Adaptive production horizon aborts with Rider 1 is not in segment 1 before first Commit. The first projected remainder leaves canonical progress just below 1.
Evidence: binary companion cases retain separate IDs
Findings.NumericalOrTraceEvidence: float:3DCCCCCD = 0.10000000149011612; float:3F666666 = 0.8999999761581421. Sum = 0.9999999776482582, residual 2.2351741790771484e-8; existing BoundaryTolerance is 1e-9. Next horizon asks segment 1 while rider remains in 0.
Findings.Confidence: High; exact operands and all seed/configuration reproductions agree.
Findings.FuturePRScope: Explicit exact intended boundary ownership for whole-segment completion, preserving path distance/time and projection parity. Keep original failing inputs; do not round them or enlarge a tolerance.

Findings.Title: Default contact consequences remain coarse compatibility rules
Findings.Expectation: Completion-grade contact consequences should follow verified physical exposure and calibrated severity while keeping legacy compatibility explicit.
Findings.Observation: A retains coarse contact eligibility/random occurrence. B supplies physical avoidance/eligibility with old authorized fallback. C supplies the impulse/recovery structure but is gated.
Findings.NumericalOrTraceEvidence: Default eligibility 0.55 m lateral and 0.12 s boundary gap; lost rhythm multiplies speed by 0.82, adds 0.20 s and may displace outward. Pilot A records two contact events; B/C record none in the same two seed-19 cases.
Findings.Confidence: High for current consumers; real-world suitability of replacement scale remains unverified.
Findings.FuturePRScope: Choose the default migration policy after correctness/calibration review; do not apply both consequence models.
Findings.Complexity: Small integration scope with substantial evidence dependency

Findings.Title: Neutral cohort speed/time amplitude needs matched calibration evidence
Findings.Expectation: Compare compatible populations and geometry before attributing maximum-speed, average-speed, L1 or spread discrepancies to production constants.
Findings.Observation: Current neutral pilot has substantially lower peak speeds than real professional Motoarena distributions while some flying laps are faster; the audit population has no professional ability mapping.
Findings.NumericalOrTraceEvidence: Pilot rider 1: max 26.501541 m/s, average 22.963825 m/s, L2 13.494101 s. Existing matched real Vmax median 113.7 km/h. Full N/P10/P25/P50/P75/P90 component comparisons and within-heat spreads are retained; no realism score.
Findings.Subsystem: Provisional drive/envelope calibration and geometry/population interpretation
Findings.Confidence: High for descriptive discrepancy; low for attribution to a specific force/envelope term.
Findings.FuturePRScope: Matched cohort/venue calibration protocol and measured context; separately select any justified parameter change after review.

Findings.Title: Endpoint impact abstraction, severity scale and one-step recovery need validation
Findings.Scenario: ordinary contacts, contact-heavy stress, controlled physiology fixtures
Findings.Expectation: Reserve/severity and disturbance duration should have compatible speedway evidence before default enablement; stress incidence must not estimate ordinary crash rate.
Findings.Observation: Impulse/ownership/recovery contracts have technical evidence. Severity boundaries, reserve factors and recovery loss map remain synthetic; recovery duration varies with the next active segment. First-touch impulse is applied to the normal segment endpoint; the traversed remainder is not reintegrated. This follows the existing documented contract and is a realism limitation, not a new contract violation.
Evidence: Applied, Pairs, Generations and Recoveries in cases.json.gz
Findings.NumericalOrTraceEvidence: Thresholds 0.35/0.70/1.05/1.55; maximum recoverable control loss 0.8 via a quadratic map; RemainingSteps = 1. Ordinary/stress severity counts and actual next-step seconds are reported separately. PGEE provides no numeric impact/recovery target. overall/19/C step 27, riders 3/4: verified touch 41.068336266334654 s; rider 3 endpoint 42.579429626464844 s, speed 18.603743 -> 19.074354 m/s, deltaV 0.47061145106830615 m/s. Impulse 69.17988330704101 N.s on each 147 kg system. Full delay/recovery distributions are in ImpactTiming/Configurations.
Findings.Subsystem: PhysicalContactAnalyzer reserve and PhysicalContactConsequenceResolver recovery mapping
Findings.Confidence: High that calibration is missing; empirical acceptable scale/duration remains unknown.
Findings.FuturePRScope: Controlled compatible impact/outcome evidence and recovery-duration assessment, preserving impulse and generation invariants. Explicitly assess the endpoint timing approximation and whether production remainder reintegration is necessary, as a separately reviewed model change.

Findings.Title: Venue and footprint boundary interpretation remain provisional
Findings.Expectation: Legal executed footprints, physical gate advantages and absolute lap targets need measured/local geometry and certified coverage.
Findings.Observation: Pilot has uncertified footprints without reference-point edge witnesses. Width reinterpretations are zero-time unswept transitions. Symmetric modeled widths/radius/start split remain approximations.
Findings.NumericalOrTraceEvidence: Three uncertified motion footprints per pilot Motoarena configuration, zero reference-point edge witnesses. Modeled mean turn width 16.6 m derives from 17.0/16.2 m; radius convention 31 m and start split 35/27 m are provisional.
Findings.Subsystem: Track geometry/reference transitions and full-footprint certification
Findings.Confidence: High for approximation/certification status; an uncertified interval alone does not prove illegal track departure.
Findings.FuturePRScope: Measure geometry/start split and inspect exact footprint boundary evidence, then review local transitions separately.

Findings.Title: Canonical gameplay launch contract is not yet migrated
Findings.Expectation: Gameplay integration must know the actual consumers; independent canonical Reaction/Start must not be assumed active when only legacy Start drives launch.
Findings.Observation: Launch uses legacy Start for reaction and force. Canonical Technique/Strength/mass/Condition have B/C consumers. Age has no direct physics multiplier; strength has no arbitrary speed bonus.
Findings.NumericalOrTraceEvidence: Reaction formula 0.28 + (0.20 - 0.28) * Start/100 s. Start 20/50/80 gives 0.264/0.24/0.216 s before IEEE representation. Compatibility Attack/Defense/Strength are 50; legacy compatibility mass is 70 kg. Longitudinal reference system mass remains 142 kg.
Findings.Confidence: High; specified future migration is not classified as a current launch implementation bug.
Findings.FuturePRScope: Explicit gameplay consumer/migration contract, controlled regressions and compatible rating evidence; preserve behavior until deliberately changed.

Findings.Title: Longer-horizon opponent strategy remains a future extension
Findings.Expectation: Assess strategic reattack/defense from actual common-time motion before adding opponent forecasts or pass bonuses.
Findings.Observation: Physical alternatives and bounded traffic responses are present. Adaptive base ranking uses a production solo horizon plus current occupancy/style/perception costs; it does not solve a complete future opponent strategy.
Findings.NumericalOrTraceEvidence: Existing response search bounds: maximum three alternatives per rider, 81 joint combinations and two response passes. Completed passes require strict executed lead transitions, never response selection alone.
Findings.Confidence: High for present scope; whether extra strategy is necessary requires product/trace review.
Findings.FuturePRScope: Evidence-led opponent-aware planning only if recorded races justify it; preserve physical pass proof and #61 bounds/performance.

Findings.Title: Exposure and intent attribution need richer passive telemetry
Findings.Expectation: Differentiate proximity, side-by-side fighting, failed requests and completed overtakes without invented exact timings.
Findings.Observation: Strict native-node lead transitions and near-interval brackets exist; precise below-threshold occupancy and causal intent-success attribution are unavailable. Summary omits full rejection matrices.
Findings.NumericalOrTraceEvidence: Pilot Motoarena C has 1051 native near-interval observations; their union is an upper bracket, not exact threshold occupancy. Competitive reach is the existing 2.5 m; ties/gaps are retained, no rider-ID ordering or epsilon is introduced.
Findings.FuturePRScope: Passive continuous exposure/intent attribution where it supports a meaningful decision; no physics changes or replacement pass rule.
